description.narrative: Denmark plans to contribute with an additional DKK 10 mio. to the SRTF as part of the Danish Peace and Stabilisation Programme for Syria Iraq 2022-2025.

The Syria Recovery Trust Fund’s (SRFT) Stabilisation Intervention in Northeast Syria (NES) "Filling the Void" (FtV) is co-funded by contributions from several countries including the United States, Denmark, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, France, Germany, and Japan. RESULTS 2022: In 2022, the SRTF provided essential aid in areas liberated from ISIS in NES, focusing on agricultural support, food security, livelihoods, WASH (water, sanitation, and hygiene), health services, and COVID-19 emergency response in Ar-Raqqa and Deir Ez-Zor Governorates. The programme "FtV" aimed to rapidly stabilise communities in these areas and involved two main stages: procurement and storage, as well as dispatch and delivery. Originally planned in three phases, it was modified in 2017 to expand its scope.
SRTF has achieved significant milestones in enhancing healthcare access and agricultural support in various governorates of Northeast Syria. They established primary health care centres, specialized medical services, and mobile clinics in Deir Ez-Zor Governorate, benefiting over 307,100 residents. Additionally, it established prosthetics centres across Northeast Syria, providing vital services and training for individuals who lost limbs due to the conflict. Furthermore, they sustained and improved comprehensive health care in Ar-Raqqa by supporting seven primary health care centres and a COVID-19 specialized hospital.
In addition to healthcare, SRTF made substantial contributions to agriculture and food security. it supported livestock farmers in Ar-Raqqa Governorate, promoting livestock production and economic resources through targeted assistance and a cost-recovery approach. SRTF also facilitated the rehabilitation of wheat mills, ensuring increased availability of flour for bakeries, benefiting an estimated 45,000 people.
